questions.prompt: Which map element helps a learner compare map distance with real ground distance?
questions.correctAnswer: Scale
questions.explanation: A scale shows the relationship between distance on a map and distance on the ground.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify map elements used to interpret distance and direction.

questions.prompt: On a map of Eastern Africa, which direction is Uganda from Kenya?
questions.correctAnswer: West
questions.explanation: Uganda lies on the western side of Kenya, so it is west of Kenya.
questions.learningOutcome: Use compass directions to describe the position of countries near Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which imaginary line crosses Kenya and helps describe its location on the globe?
questions.correctAnswer: Equator
questions.explanation: The Equator passes through Kenya and helps show that Kenya lies near the middle of the globe.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify lines used to describe the location of Kenya and Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which water body borders the south-eastern part of Kenya?
questions.correctAnswer: Indian Ocean
questions.explanation: Kenya has a coastline along the Indian Ocean in the south-eastern part of the country.
questions.learningOutcome: Locate Kenya in relation to major neighbouring physical features.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to find countries that border Kenya. Which source would be most useful?
questions.correctAnswer: An atlas showing political maps
questions.explanation: A political map in an atlas shows country boundaries and helps learners identify neighbouring countries.
questions.learningOutcome: Use maps and atlases to locate countries in Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which country borders Kenya to the north?
questions.correctAnswer: Ethiopia
questions.explanation: Ethiopia is found north of Kenya, while Tanzania is south of Kenya.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify countries that border Kenya using compass directions.

questions.prompt: Which type of map is best for showing mountains, lakes, rivers, and valleys?
questions.correctAnswer: Physical map
questions.explanation: A physical map shows natural features such as mountains, rivers, lakes, plains, and valleys.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable maps for studying physical features.

questions.prompt: Why should a map have a key or legend?
options: To explain the meaning of symbols used on the map
To replace all place names on the map
To show only the age of the map reader
questions.correctAnswer: To explain the meaning of symbols used on the map
questions.explanation: A key explains symbols such as roads, rivers, forests, schools, and boundaries.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret simple map symbols using a key.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains why Eastern African countries need good relations?
options: They share trade, transport routes, security concerns, and natural resources
They should stop all people from travelling
They have no need for cooperation
They can remove all borders from maps
questions.correctAnswer: They share trade, transport routes, security concerns, and natural resources
questions.explanation: Neighbouring countries benefit when they cooperate in trade, transport, security, and environmental care.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why countries in Eastern Africa cooperate with one another.

questions.prompt: A class wants to compare the size of Kenya with Tanzania and Uganda. Which method is best?
options: Use an atlas or reliable map with area information
Guess by looking at classroom walls
questions.correctAnswer: Use an atlas or reliable map with area information
questions.explanation: An atlas or reliable map gives boundaries and area information that can be used for comparison.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze map information to compare countries in Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which lake is shared by Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania?
questions.correctAnswer: Lake Victoria
questions.explanation: Lake Victoria is a large freshwater lake shared by Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania.
questions.subStrandTitle: Major Physical Features in Eastern Africa
questions.learningOutcome: Identify major lakes found in Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which major valley system passes through parts of Kenya and other Eastern African countries?
questions.correctAnswer: Great Rift Valley
questions.explanation: The Great Rift Valley is a major physical feature that runs through Kenya and other parts of Eastern Africa.
questions.subStrandTitle: Major Physical Features in Eastern Africa
questions.learningOutcome: Describe major physical features found in Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Why are highland areas in Kenya important for farming?
options: They often have cooler temperatures, fertile soils, and reliable rainfall
They are always too dry for crops
They have no roads or markets
They are made only of bare rock
questions.correctAnswer: They often have cooler temperatures, fertile soils, and reliable rainfall
questions.explanation: Many highland areas support crops such as tea and vegetables because of climate and soil conditions.
questions.subStrandTitle: Major Physical Features in Eastern Africa
questions.learningOutcome: Relate physical features to human activities in Kenya and Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which activity is commonly supported by lakes and rivers in Eastern Africa?
questions.correctAnswer: Fishing
questions.explanation: Lakes and rivers provide fish, water for domestic use, irrigation, transport in some places, and recreation.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify economic uses of lakes and rivers in Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which action best protects a river used by a community?
options: Planting trees along the river bank
Dumping plastic waste into the river
Washing chemicals directly in the river
Clearing all vegetation near the river
questions.correctAnswer: Planting trees along the river bank
questions.explanation: Trees along river banks reduce erosion, protect water sources, and keep the river environment healthier.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify ways of conserving water bodies and nearby land.

questions.prompt: What is soil erosion?
options: The removal of topsoil by water, wind, or human activity
The growth of crops in fertile soil
The careful storage of clean water
questions.correctAnswer: The removal of topsoil by water, wind, or human activity
questions.explanation: Soil erosion happens when fertile topsoil is carried away, reducing the land's usefulness.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe causes and effects of soil erosion.

questions.prompt: A farmer plants crops across a slope instead of straight down the slope. Which problem is the farmer reducing?
questions.correctAnswer: Soil erosion
questions.explanation: Planting across a slope slows runoff water and helps stop soil from being washed away.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply soil conservation practices to farming situations.

questions.prompt: Which physical feature is a broad flat or gently rolling area of land?
questions.correctAnswer: Plain
questions.explanation: A plain is a broad area of flat or gently rolling land and may support farming, settlement, or grazing.
questions.subStrandTitle: Major Physical Features in Eastern Africa
questions.learningOutcome: Identify and describe common physical features.

questions.prompt: Why should learners avoid littering during a visit to a lake shore?
options: Litter can pollute water and harm living things
Litter makes all maps more accurate
questions.correctAnswer: Litter can pollute water and harm living things
questions.explanation: Keeping lake shores clean protects water, fish, birds, and the people who use the lake.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate responsible behaviour during visits to physical features.

questions.prompt: A class wants to present mountains, lakes, and rivers of Eastern Africa. Which product best fits the task?
options: A labelled sketch map with a key and title
A list of lunch items only
questions.correctAnswer: A labelled sketch map with a key and title
questions.explanation: A labelled sketch map can show the location of physical features clearly and can include map elements.
questions.subStrandTitle: Major Physical Features in Eastern Africa
questions.learningOutcome: Create a simple representation of major physical features.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes climate?
options: The usual weather pattern of a place over many years
The weather at one moment only
The shape of a country boundary
The number of houses in a town
questions.correctAnswer: The usual weather pattern of a place over many years
questions.explanation: Climate refers to long-term weather patterns, while weather can change within hours or days.
questions.learningOutcome: Differentiate between weather and climate.

questions.prompt: Which condition is common in many semi-arid areas of Kenya?
options: Rain every day of the year
questions.correctAnswer: Low rainfall
questions.explanation: Semi-arid areas receive low and unreliable rainfall, so people often adapt their activities to dry conditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe features of different climate regions in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which vegetation type has grass with scattered trees and is common in parts of Eastern Africa?
questions.correctAnswer: Savanna
questions.explanation: Savanna vegetation has grass and scattered trees, and it supports grazing and wildlife in many areas.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common vegetation types in Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Where are mangrove forests most likely to grow in Kenya?
questions.correctAnswer: Along sheltered coastal areas
questions.explanation: Mangroves grow in salty coastal wetlands and help protect shorelines and fish breeding areas.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe vegetation found in coastal environments.

questions.prompt: Which human activity can lead to loss of forest cover?
questions.correctAnswer: Cutting trees carelessly for charcoal
questions.explanation: Careless cutting of trees reduces forest cover and can lead to soil erosion, loss of habitats, and lower rainfall protection.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain human activities that damage vegetation.

questions.prompt: Which action best shows afforestation?
options: Planting trees in an area where there were few or no trees
questions.correctAnswer: Planting trees in an area where there were few or no trees
questions.explanation: Afforestation means establishing trees in an area that did not have enough tree cover.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify ways of increasing and conserving vegetation cover.

questions.prompt: How can drought affect pastoral communities?
options: It can reduce pasture and water for livestock
It stops the need for water
questions.correctAnswer: It can reduce pasture and water for livestock
questions.explanation: Drought reduces rainfall, which can lower pasture growth and water availability for animals and people.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how climate affects ways of life in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which crop is commonly linked with cool and wet highland areas in Kenya?
questions.correctAnswer: Tea
questions.explanation: Tea grows well in cool, wet highland areas with suitable soils.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate climate conditions to crops grown in Kenya.

questions.prompt: A weather record shows little rainfall for several weeks. Which activity should a school promote?
options: Saving water and using it carefully
Washing all floors with wasteful amounts of water
questions.correctAnswer: Saving water and using it carefully
questions.explanation: During dry periods, people should conserve water and avoid waste so that essential needs are met.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply weather information to daily decision-making.

questions.prompt: Which class project best shows the link between climate and human activities?
options: A chart matching rainfall and temperature patterns with farming, fishing, and pastoralism
A list of favourite colours only
A drawing of one desk without labels
A count of school shoes only
questions.correctAnswer: A chart matching rainfall and temperature patterns with farming, fishing, and pastoralism
questions.explanation: A comparison chart can show how different climate conditions influence the activities people choose.
questions.learningOutcome: Create presentations showing how climate affects human activities.

questions.prompt: What does population distribution mean?
options: How people are spread over an area
questions.correctAnswer: How people are spread over an area
questions.explanation: Population distribution describes where people live and how closely or widely they are spread.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the meaning of population distribution.

questions.prompt: Which factor can make an area densely populated?
options: Reliable water, fertile soils, jobs, and services
No water and no roads at all
Only bare rock and no services
questions.correctAnswer: Reliable water, fertile soils, jobs, and services
questions.explanation: People often settle where they can find water, food, work, transport, schools, health care, and security.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify factors influencing population distribution.

questions.prompt: Why are some dry areas sparsely populated?
options: Low rainfall can limit farming and water supply
Every dry area has the largest cities
Dry areas always have more water than highlands
People cannot travel in dry areas
questions.correctAnswer: Low rainfall can limit farming and water supply
questions.explanation: Low rainfall and limited water can make farming, settlement, and livestock keeping more difficult.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how climate affects where people settle.

questions.prompt: A settlement develops along a main road. Which settlement pattern does this best show?
questions.correctAnswer: Linear settlement
questions.explanation: A linear settlement is arranged in a line, often along a road, river, railway, or coastline.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common settlement patterns and their causes.

questions.prompt: Which term describes people moving from one place to another to live for some time?
questions.correctAnswer: Migration
questions.explanation: Migration is the movement of people from one place to another for settlement, work, education, safety, or other reasons.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the meaning of migration.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of a pull factor in migration?
options: Availability of jobs in a town
questions.correctAnswer: Availability of jobs in a town
questions.explanation: A pull factor attracts people to a place, while drought, floods, and insecurity can push people away.
questions.learningOutcome: Differentiate between push and pull factors in migration.

questions.prompt: What is a census mainly used for?
options: Counting people and gathering population information
Measuring the length of a river only
Cooking food for a school event
questions.correctAnswer: Counting people and gathering population information
questions.explanation: A census helps a country know its population size and plan services such as schools, hospitals, roads, and water.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of population data in planning.

questions.prompt: If a small area has many people living close together, how can it be described?
questions.correctAnswer: Densely populated
questions.explanation: An area is densely populated when many people live in a small space.
questions.learningOutcome: Use population vocabulary to describe settlement.

questions.prompt: Which problem can rapid growth of a town cause if services do not improve?
options: Overcrowding and pressure on water, housing, and transport
questions.correctAnswer: Overcrowding and pressure on water, housing, and transport
questions.explanation: When towns grow quickly, services must also grow or people may face overcrowding and shortages.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze effects of population growth in urban areas.

questions.prompt: Which plan best helps a growing town serve its residents better?
options: Improve water supply, waste collection, housing, schools, and transport
questions.correctAnswer: Improve water supply, waste collection, housing, schools, and transport
questions.explanation: Good planning uses population information to provide services that meet people's needs.
questions.learningOutcome: Create simple plans for improving services in growing settlements.

questions.prompt: What is culture?
options: The way of life of a people
Only the shape of a river
questions.correctAnswer: The way of life of a people
questions.explanation: Culture includes language, food, dress, beliefs, values, music, dance, stories, and ways of doing things.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the meaning of culture.

questions.prompt: Which item is an example of cultural heritage?
options: A traditional song taught by elders
A broken plastic bag on a road
questions.correctAnswer: A traditional song taught by elders
questions.explanation: Cultural heritage includes traditions, songs, stories, dances, tools, foods, and places passed from one generation to another.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify examples of cultural heritage in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which behaviour shows respect for cultural diversity in class?
options: Listening politely when learners share different traditions
Refusing to work with learners from other communities
questions.correctAnswer: Listening politely when learners share different traditions
questions.explanation: Respect for diversity means treating people fairly and learning from differences without insults or stereotypes.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate respect for different cultures in school.

questions.prompt: Why is national unity important in Kenya?
options: It helps people from different communities live and work together peacefully
It teaches people to dislike other communities
It stops citizens from helping one another
It removes the need for respect
questions.correctAnswer: It helps people from different communities live and work together peacefully
questions.explanation: National unity supports peace, cooperation, fairness, and a shared sense of belonging.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of national unity.

questions.prompt: Which set contains examples of language groups found in Kenya?
questions.correctAnswer: Bantu, Nilotic, and Cushitic
questions.explanation: Bantu, Nilotic, and Cushitic are broad language groups represented among communities in Kenya.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify broad language groups found in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which situation best shows interdependence among communities?
options: Farmers sell food to town residents while town traders supply tools and services
Everyone refuses to trade or share skills
questions.correctAnswer: Farmers sell food to town residents while town traders supply tools and services
questions.explanation: Interdependence means people and communities rely on one another for goods, services, skills, and support.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how communities depend on one another.

questions.prompt: How can cultural festivals help a community?
options: They can preserve heritage and promote respect among people
They make every person speak one language only
questions.correctAnswer: They can preserve heritage and promote respect among people
questions.explanation: Cultural festivals can teach history, celebrate identity, encourage tourism, and promote understanding.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of cultural activities in society.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Kenyan communities is most respectful?
options: Every community should be treated with dignity and fairness
Only one community has useful traditions
It is acceptable to insult another culture
Stereotypes help people understand others well
questions.correctAnswer: Every community should be treated with dignity and fairness
questions.explanation: Respectful learning avoids stereotypes and recognizes that all people deserve dignity and fairness.
questions.learningOutcome: Promote respectful attitudes towards cultural diversity.

questions.prompt: Which role did elders often play in many traditional Kenyan communities?
options: Advising people and helping settle disputes
questions.correctAnswer: Advising people and helping settle disputes
questions.explanation: Elders often guided community decisions, advised families, preserved knowledge, and helped solve disputes.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe roles of traditional leaders and elders.

questions.prompt: A class wants to learn about a local cultural practice respectfully. Which activity is best?
options: Interview knowledgeable community members and record information politely
Invent false stories about the community
Ignore permission and take private items
questions.correctAnswer: Interview knowledgeable community members and record information politely
questions.explanation: Respectful interviews help learners collect accurate information while showing courtesy to community members.
questions.learningOutcome: Create respectful inquiry projects about local cultural heritage.

questions.prompt: Which is a natural resource?
questions.correctAnswer: Forest
questions.explanation: A natural resource comes from the environment. Forests, water, minerals, soil, and wildlife are examples.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify examples of natural resources in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which resource can be renewable if managed well?
questions.correctAnswer: Forest trees
questions.explanation: Trees can regrow when people plant, protect, and harvest them responsibly.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish renewable resources from non-renewable or manufactured items.

questions.prompt: Which economic activity involves growing crops and keeping animals?
questions.correctAnswer: Agriculture
questions.explanation: Agriculture includes crop farming and livestock keeping for food, income, and raw materials.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify main economic activities in Kenya and Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Why is fishing important around Lake Victoria?
options: It provides food and income for many households
It stops all trade in towns
It replaces the need for schools
questions.correctAnswer: It provides food and income for many households
questions.explanation: Fishing supports food supply, jobs, trade, and related activities in communities near the lake.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of fishing to communities near water bodies.

questions.prompt: Which activity is linked to tourists visiting national parks and historic sites?
questions.correctAnswer: Tourism
questions.explanation: Tourism involves people travelling to places such as parks, beaches, museums, and cultural sites for learning or recreation.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify tourism as an economic activity.

questions.prompt: How can good transport improve trade?
options: It helps goods and people move faster between places
It stops all goods from reaching markets
It removes the need for cooperation
questions.correctAnswer: It helps goods and people move faster between places
questions.explanation: Roads, railways, air transport, and water transport help connect producers, traders, and consumers.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of transport in trade and development.

questions.prompt: A farmer joins a cooperative society. Which benefit is most likely?
options: Members can market produce together and access support
Members lose the right to sell crops
questions.correctAnswer: Members can market produce together and access support
questions.explanation: Cooperatives can help farmers pool produce, get better prices, save money, and access services.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how cooperatives support economic activities.

questions.prompt: Which practice shows sustainable use of a forest?
options: Harvesting selected trees and planting replacements
Cutting every tree and leaving bare land
Burning the whole forest for charcoal
questions.correctAnswer: Harvesting selected trees and planting replacements
questions.explanation: Sustainable use meets present needs while protecting resources for the future.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply sustainable practices to natural resource use.

questions.prompt: Which problem can occur when people overfish a lake?
options: Fish numbers can reduce and future catches can fall
questions.correctAnswer: Fish numbers can reduce and future catches can fall
questions.explanation: Overfishing removes too many fish and can harm future food supply and livelihoods.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze effects of misusing natural resources.

questions.prompt: Which plan best supports both tourism and environmental protection in a park?
options: Guide visitors, manage waste, protect habitats, and involve local communities
questions.correctAnswer: Guide visitors, manage waste, protect habitats, and involve local communities
questions.explanation: Responsible tourism protects the environment while helping visitors learn and communities benefit.
questions.learningOutcome: Create responsible tourism plans that protect natural and cultural resources.

questions.prompt: Who is a citizen of Kenya?
options: A person who legally belongs to Kenya
A river that flows through Kenya
A road sign near a market
questions.correctAnswer: A person who legally belongs to Kenya
questions.explanation: A citizen legally belongs to a country and has rights and responsibilities in that country.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the meaning of citizenship.

questions.prompt: Which pair correctly matches a right with a responsibility?
options: Right to education - responsibility to attend school and learn
Right to safety - responsibility to bully others
Right to health - responsibility to spread disease
Right to property - responsibility to steal
questions.correctAnswer: Right to education - responsibility to attend school and learn
questions.explanation: Rights should be enjoyed while respecting responsibilities and the rights of others.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate rights to responsibilities in daily life.

questions.prompt: Which is a national symbol of Kenya?
questions.correctAnswer: National flag
questions.explanation: National symbols such as the flag, national anthem, and coat of arms represent the country and its values.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify national symbols and their importance.

questions.prompt: Which action shows patriotism at school?
options: Respecting national symbols and serving the community
questions.correctAnswer: Respecting national symbols and serving the community
questions.explanation: Patriotism includes love for one's country, respect for national symbols, and responsible service.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate patriotic behaviour in school and community life.

questions.prompt: Two learners disagree over a shared book. Which response best promotes peace?
options: Listen to each other and agree on fair turns
questions.correctAnswer: Listen to each other and agree on fair turns
questions.explanation: Peaceful conflict resolution uses listening, respect, fairness, apology, and agreement on solutions.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply peaceful ways of solving disagreements.

questions.prompt: Which value helps people live peacefully in a diverse society?
questions.correctAnswer: Tolerance
questions.explanation: Tolerance means respecting differences and allowing people to live together peacefully.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify values that promote peace and unity.

questions.prompt: What should a child do if they feel unsafe or are being mistreated?
options: Report to a trusted adult such as a teacher, parent, or guardian
Keep silent even when in danger
questions.correctAnswer: Report to a trusted adult such as a teacher, parent, or guardian
questions.explanation: Reporting to a trusted adult helps protect the child and allows responsible people to respond safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify safe ways of protecting children from harm.

questions.prompt: Which behaviour shows integrity?
options: Returning a lost book to the teacher
questions.correctAnswer: Returning a lost book to the teacher
questions.explanation: Integrity means being honest and doing the right thing even when no one is watching.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply values of good citizenship in school situations.

questions.prompt: Which action shows care for public property?
options: Using school desks carefully and reporting damage
questions.correctAnswer: Using school desks carefully and reporting damage
questions.explanation: Public property belongs to the community, so citizens should use it responsibly and protect it from damage.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate responsible use of public property.

questions.prompt: Which community service activity can learners safely take part in with guidance?
options: Cleaning a school compound and sorting waste
questions.correctAnswer: Cleaning a school compound and sorting waste
questions.explanation: Community service helps learners practise responsibility, cooperation, cleanliness, and care for shared spaces.
questions.learningOutcome: Participate responsibly in community service activities.

questions.prompt: What is a constitution?
options: The basic law that guides how a country is governed
A type of rainfall in highlands
A map symbol for a mountain
questions.correctAnswer: The basic law that guides how a country is governed
questions.explanation: A constitution sets out rights, responsibilities, government structure, and rules for leadership.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the meaning and purpose of a constitution.

questions.prompt: Which set names the three arms of Kenya's national government?
questions.correctAnswer: Executive, Legislature, and Judiciary
questions.explanation: The national government has the executive, legislature, and judiciary, each with different duties.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the three arms of national government.

questions.prompt: Which arm of government makes laws?
questions.correctAnswer: Legislature
questions.explanation: The legislature, which includes Parliament, makes laws and represents citizens.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of the legislature.

questions.prompt: Which arm of government interprets laws and settles legal disputes?
questions.correctAnswer: Judiciary
questions.explanation: The judiciary includes courts that interpret laws and help settle legal disputes fairly.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of the judiciary.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the executive arm of government?
options: It implements laws and runs government services
It records daily classroom weather only
It sells fish in all markets
questions.correctAnswer: It implements laws and runs government services
questions.explanation: The executive puts laws and policies into action and manages many public services.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe functions of the executive arm of government.

questions.prompt: Which service is a county government commonly expected to support?
questions.correctAnswer: Local health services and markets
questions.explanation: County governments help provide local services such as health facilities, markets, county roads, and sanitation.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify services provided by county governments.

questions.prompt: Who leads the county executive in Kenya?
questions.correctAnswer: Governor
questions.explanation: A governor leads the county executive and works with other county leaders to serve residents.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify key leaders in county government.

questions.prompt: What is one role of a Member of County Assembly?
options: Representing people from a ward in county matters
questions.correctAnswer: Representing people from a ward in county matters
questions.explanation: Members of County Assembly represent wards, make county laws, and check county government work.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe roles of elected county representatives.

questions.prompt: Why is public participation important in county planning?
options: It allows residents to share views before decisions are made
It hides plans from the public
It makes leaders ignore local needs
questions.correctAnswer: It allows residents to share views before decisions are made
questions.explanation: Public participation helps leaders understand local needs and make decisions with the people affected.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze the importance of public participation in governance.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of voting in an election?
options: To choose leaders or make decisions fairly
questions.correctAnswer: To choose leaders or make decisions fairly
questions.explanation: Voting gives eligible people a peaceful and fair way to choose leaders or decide on issues.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the purpose of voting in democratic processes.

questions.prompt: Which quality is most important for a good leader?
questions.correctAnswer: Honesty
questions.explanation: Good leaders should be honest, fair, responsible, respectful, and ready to serve others.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify qualities of good leadership.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains devolution in Kenya?
options: Sharing some government powers and services with county governments
Removing all local services from counties
Letting one school make laws for the whole country
Stopping citizens from using county offices
questions.correctAnswer: Sharing some government powers and services with county governments
questions.explanation: Devolution brings some services and decision-making closer to people through county governments.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the meaning and importance of devolution.

questions.prompt: What is democracy?
options: A way of governing where people participate fairly
A method of hiding public views
A rule that only one person speaks always
A map symbol for a lake
questions.correctAnswer: A way of governing where people participate fairly
questions.explanation: Democracy allows people to participate, choose leaders, share views, and respect fair decisions.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the meaning of democracy.

questions.prompt: Which class decision shows democracy?
options: Learners suggest options, discuss respectfully, and vote
One learner secretly chooses for everyone
The loudest learner blocks all views
questions.correctAnswer: Learners suggest options, discuss respectfully, and vote
questions.explanation: Democratic decision-making includes participation, respect, fairness, and acceptance of agreed results.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply democratic decision-making in school situations.

questions.prompt: Which action respects the views of a minority group after a vote?
options: Listening to their concerns and treating them fairly
Insulting them for losing the vote
Refusing to let them speak again
questions.correctAnswer: Listening to their concerns and treating them fairly
questions.explanation: Democracy should respect both the decision of the majority and the rights and dignity of minority groups.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze how fairness and respect support democratic practice.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of a human right?
questions.correctAnswer: Right to education
questions.explanation: Human rights are basic protections and freedoms, such as education, safety, health, and dignity.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify examples of human rights.

questions.prompt: Which behaviour respects another learner's right to dignity?
options: Laughing when the learner needs help
questions.correctAnswer: Speaking politely and avoiding insults
questions.explanation: Respecting dignity means treating others with kindness, privacy, fairness, and respect.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply respect for human rights in school situations.

questions.prompt: Which benefit can regional cooperation bring to Eastern African countries?
options: Improved trade, transport, peace, and shared problem solving
No need to protect shared resources
questions.correctAnswer: Improved trade, transport, peace, and shared problem solving
questions.explanation: Regional cooperation helps neighbouring countries address issues that cross borders and support development.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain benefits of cooperation among countries in Eastern Africa.

questions.prompt: Which issue is best solved through cooperation between neighbouring countries?
options: Protecting a shared lake from pollution
questions.correctAnswer: Protecting a shared lake from pollution
questions.explanation: Shared resources such as lakes, rivers, wildlife, and transport routes need cooperation across borders.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze regional issues that require cooperation.

questions.prompt: Which online behaviour shows responsible citizenship?
questions.correctAnswer: Sharing respectful and truthful messages
questions.explanation: Responsible citizens communicate respectfully and avoid harmful, false, or private information.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply good citizenship values to digital communication.

questions.prompt: Heavy rain causes flooding near a school path. Which action is safest for learners?
options: Use a safer route and report the danger to adults
questions.correctAnswer: Use a safer route and report the danger to adults
questions.explanation: Floodwater can be dangerous, so learners should avoid it and report hazards to trusted adults.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safety measures during weather-related hazards.

questions.prompt: Which question would best guide a study of population and environment in a town?
options: How does population growth affect water, waste, housing, and transport?
What colour is one school bag?
Which desk is nearest the window?
How many times did one bell ring today?
questions.correctAnswer: How does population growth affect water, waste, housing, and transport?
questions.explanation: A good inquiry question focuses on relationships between population growth and community services.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze links between population growth and environmental pressure.

questions.prompt: Which statement best compares pastoralism and crop farming?
options: Pastoralism focuses on livestock, while crop farming focuses on growing crops
Both are only forms of fishing
Crop farming means moving with cattle only
Pastoralism means planting tea in factories
questions.correctAnswer: Pastoralism focuses on livestock, while crop farming focuses on growing crops
questions.explanation: Pastoralists keep livestock, while crop farmers grow plants for food, sale, or raw materials.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare different forms of agriculture in Kenya.

questions.prompt: Which action is most likely to reduce waste pollution in a market centre?
options: Provide bins, sort waste, and organize regular collection
Throw all waste into nearby rivers
Burn all waste beside food stalls
questions.correctAnswer: Provide bins, sort waste, and organize regular collection
questions.explanation: Waste management works better when people reduce, sort, store, and collect waste safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze practical solutions to waste pollution.

questions.prompt: Which message best encourages environmental conservation at school?
options: Plant trees, save water, and keep our compound clean
Leave taps open and waste water
questions.correctAnswer: Plant trees, save water, and keep our compound clean
questions.explanation: A conservation message should encourage practical actions that protect land, water, plants, and shared spaces.
questions.learningOutcome: Create messages that promote environmental conservation.

questions.prompt: A community has limited money for a water project. Which decision-making step is most responsible?
options: Discuss needs, compare options, and choose the project that helps many people fairly
Let one person secretly use all the money
Ignore the most urgent water needs
questions.correctAnswer: Discuss needs, compare options, and choose the project that helps many people fairly
questions.explanation: Responsible public decisions should be fair, transparent, based on needs, and supported by records.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate fair use of public resources in community situations.

questions.prompt: Which source is most reliable for confirming the location of a county boundary?
options: An official or up-to-date map from a trusted source
A rumour heard at the market
A guess made without a map
A song that does not mention counties
questions.correctAnswer: An official or up-to-date map from a trusted source
questions.explanation: Reliable information should come from trusted sources, especially when checking boundaries, locations, and facts.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate sources of geographical information for reliability.

questions.prompt: A class is preparing a cultural heritage display. Which plan is most respectful?
options: Use accurate information, ask permission, label items, and avoid stereotypes
Mix false information with real names
questions.correctAnswer: Use accurate information, ask permission, label items, and avoid stereotypes
questions.explanation: Respectful heritage displays protect dignity, accuracy, permission, and fairness.
questions.learningOutcome: Create respectful presentations about cultural heritage.

questions.prompt: Which plan best promotes peace during a school sports competition?
options: Agree on rules, respect referees, cheer politely, and accept results
questions.correctAnswer: Agree on rules, respect referees, cheer politely, and accept results
questions.explanation: Peaceful competition needs clear rules, respect, self-control, fairness, and acceptance of outcomes.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyze actions that promote peace in group activities.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to design a simple community action project. Which project best combines citizenship and environmental care?
options: Organize a guided clean-up, plant trees, and report progress to the school
Throw waste in drains and leave immediately
Cut young trees to make space for litter
Stop classmates from joining service activities
questions.correctAnswer: Organize a guided clean-up, plant trees, and report progress to the school
questions.explanation: A good action project is safe, useful, organized, and shows responsibility for people and the environment.
questions.learningOutcome: Create simple community action plans that show responsible citizenship.
